A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 18-page versions of the same HyperDAS paper, including Appendices A.1–A.7. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of all dimensions.

before.justification: v1 reports original HyperDAS experiments on RAVEL with Llama3-8B, including benchmark results, intervention analyses, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original RAVEL experiments, numerical results, intervention analyses, and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The concept encoder, token-pair selection, Householder-based subspace construction, losses, masking, and inference procedure are unchanged. Text moving between opening pages does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five RAVEL domains: cities, Nobel laureates, occupations, physical objects, and verbs. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: MDAS remains the baseline in Figure 3, and Figure 11 retains the same HyperDAS, MDAS, and sparse-autoencoder comparison. Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: The target model, metrics, layer evaluations, masking procedures, training settings, and discrete intervention evaluation are unchanged. Appendix A retains identical train/test counts, disjoint-prompt splits, and five-epoch training.

E4.justification: The layer-location, sparsity, symmetry, and Householder-vector analyses are unchanged. Appendices A.3–A.7 retain the same shortcut example, initialization comparison, feature-size analysis, component ablations, and intervention demonstrations.

E5.justification: Statistical and uncertainty reporting is identical. No seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are unchanged. Figure 3a retains average Disentangle scores of 76.0 for MDAS and 84.7 for asymmetric HyperDAS; the appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations, including distributed interventions, the Householder transformation, losses, and discrete alignment rules, are unchanged. No mathematical reasoning or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about automating concept localization and achieving state-of-the-art RAVEL performance. The added code pointer does not revise the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations of intervention behavior, computational tradeoffs, and faithfulness concerns are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitation to linearly mediated concepts and the warning about supervised interpretability producing false positives.

D1.justification: v2 adds a 'Code available at' statement and a HyperDAS GitHub repository address to the abstract, absent from v1. This supplies new code-access information; implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior interpretability methods are unchanged. The Background section moves across a page boundary without substantive revision.

P1.justification: The abstract gains a short code-availability statement, and the arXiv version/date marking changes. Otherwise, the prose, terminology, and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded abstract causes limited text reflow across pages 1–5, including moving the first introductory list item onto page 2. Figures, tables, and captions are unchanged; pages 6–18 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer modestly improves code discoverability and reproducibility documentation. Scientific content and supporting evidence, including the appendices, are unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, but not the repository's completeness or usability.
